diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepresent actions whose result is explicitly marked repeated, indicating persistence with non-progressing behavior.
expected_mechanism: Detecting repeated outcomes and forcing reassessment should reduce unproductive loops and encourage alternative actions. Cost: extra state tracking and occasional unnecessary replanning when repetition is intentional.
policy_text: Track recent action outcomes. When an action produces the same non-progress result twice, stop repeating it, reassess the current state and objective, then choose a materially different action or explicitly terminate if no justified alternative remains.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[(if .value>0 then "candidate/bad" else "base/good" end),.stack_frames[0],(.value|if .<0 then -. else . end)]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{all[$1]+=$3;if($2=="result:repeated")rep[$1]+=$3} END{for(k in all)printf "%s repeated=%d total=%d share=%.2f%%\n",k,rep[k],all[k],100*rep[k]/all[k]}' | sort
quantitative_evidence.finding: Candidate/bad: 1,485 of 7,366 operations were repeated (20.16%); base/good: 224 of 3,780 (5.93%). The candidate/bad repeated-operation share was 3.40× higher, with a signed excess of 1,261 operations.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated") | [(if .value>0 then "candidate/bad" else "base/good" end),.labels.source_session[0]]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | sort -u | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated outcomes occurred in 88 distinct candidate/bad source sessions versus 20 distinct base/good source sessions, showing recurrence beyond a single trajectory.
